title: Definition of the Fare That Bands the Change Fee
content:
**Revenue accounting definition — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** The fare that bands the change fee is measured by one of three conventions:

| Ticket | Fare that bands the change fee |
|---|---|
| Names an active corporate agreement | The fare collected less the ticket's taxes and fees: the negotiated fare before taxes |
| Any other ticket with at least one flown coupon | The fare still unflown: the fare collected less the coupon value already flown |
| Any other ticket | The fare collected: every fare-collection and add-collect entry |

The first row applies to a ticket naming an active agreement whether or not a coupon has been flown. The ticket's taxes and fees are those recorded on the ticket; the coupon value already flown is every flown-coupon entry on it.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

| Ticket | Fare collected | Taxes and fees | Coupon value flown | Fare that bands the fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Active agreement, nothing flown | 720.00 | 96.00 | 0 | 624.00 |
| Active agreement, one coupon flown | 720.00 | 96.00 | 300.00 | 624.00 |
| No agreement, one coupon flown | 720.00 | 96.00 | 300.00 | 420.00 |
| No agreement, nothing flown | 720.00 | 96.00 | 0 | 720.00 |
